I estimated the average treatment effect on the control group (ATC) by fitting a linear regression of the outcome `y` on all 25 covariates, using treated units only. I then predicted what each control unit's outcome would have been under treatment and averaged the difference from their observed outcomes. This gives about **11.61**.

The data contain only observed outcomes, so this is a model-based estimate, and it depends on the linear outcome model being adequate. A single pooled regression with a treatment dummy gives a much lower figure of 4.76. That model assumes the effect is the same for everyone, and the gap suggests the effect varies with the covariates. I went with the treated-only model because it targets the control group's effect directly.

ANSWER: 11.61
